messages:
anita: FYI support opened an emergency ticket: multiple customers reporting 502/504 + TLS handshake failures to hosted inference around 14:05 UTC. Links: ticket RT-5610, sample curl + HAR attached.
tom: seeing SLO alert too: hosted-infer 5xx rate > 20% for 5m. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.io/dashboards/hosted-infer/errors
rafael: quick glance at gateway logs shows a spike in `tls_handshake_timeout` and `upstream reset` to some runtime pods at 14:04-14:10.
meera: any recent deploys? I see runtime-pool autoscaled earlier today. No code deploys in last 24h.
support-jordan: customer reported this started right after they updated billing plan via the console. They rolled it back and errors decreased but resurfaced later. Their repro: 50 concurrent short generate requests -> ~8% 502 within 90s.
tom: run log query for that tenant window to capture status distribution:
```
index=prod-logs service=gateway
| where tenant_id="acct_Y9"
| where timestamp between ("2024-10-03T14:00:00Z" .. "2024-10-03T14:20:00Z")
| parse message with * "status=" status:int " "*
| stats count() by status, backend_node
```
rafael: results: majority 200 from runtime-09/10, but runtime-04 shows a large number of 502 and several 504. Runtime-04 also shows a pileup of connections: `accept queue overflow` in kernel logs.
meera: kernel note + tls handshake timeouts -> could be too many sockets in SYN/handshake states, maybe workers blocked. Check runtime-04 process logs for stuck threads or goroutine dumps.
anita: grabbing trace samples. Some traces for failing requests show no runtime span emitted; trace stops at gateway. TraceID examples: trace-b2c3d4, trace-b2c3d9.
sam_oncall_bot: alert: SLO burn escalated to P1 at 14:07 UTC (5xx high). Paging oncall.
tom: temporary mitigation: create traffic steering rule to avoid runtime-04 and drain it. Applying now.
meera: also limit concurrent in-flight per-tenant to 30 for hosted pool to avoid queue storms while we debug. Can we patch the rate limiter?
rafael: put in a routing override: `route-override tenant=acct_Y9 avoid_nodes=runtime-04` 14:12 UTC (id r-6621). Also set per-tenant concurrency cap to 30 (effective immediately).
support-jordan: customer confirms errors dropped after you applied the cap and avoided runtime-04. Appreciative.
anita: pulled runtime-04 logs: several repeated stacktraces around 14:04 in the runtime worker thread. Snippet: 
```
2024-10-03T14:04:07Z runtime-04 ERROR worker.go: panic: nil pointer deref
goroutine 88 [running]:
  github.com/redwood/infer.(*worker).handleRequest(...)
  /src/runtime/worker.go:412
2024-10-03T14:04:07Z runtime-04 WARN supervisor: worker 88 crashed, restarting
2024-10-03T14:04:08Z runtime-04 INFO metrics: queue_depth=186
```
meera: queue_depth 186 is high; that's consistent with accept queue overflow. Was there any GC surge or native memory pressure?
tom: host metrics show memory stable but thread count spiked then crashed. Could be a lock contention bug with the billing client call.
rafael: I grep the logs for billing calls: there are blocking calls to billing-api that take ~4-6s during that window. Those calls are synchronous in the request path for token validation/entitlements on this tenant. If many requests hit at once, workers block and queue.
anita: that fits: billing slow -> worker threads block -> connection pileup -> TLS handshake timeouts on new connections -> gateway returns 504 or 502 when upstream closes.
sam_oncall_bot: note: we have unresolved traces missing runtime spans because worker died mid-request. That explains trace gaps.
meera: immediate actions:
- short-term: keep routing override + tenant concurrency cap until runtime patch (anita)
- mid-term: add circuit breaker/timeouts to billing client and make entitlement check async where possible (rafael)
- triage: capture a goroutine dump and core when we can repro, collect kernel accept queue stats (meera)
tom: run a search to see if other tenants hit the same code path heavily:
```
index=prod-logs service=runtime
| where message contains "billing-check" and timestamp > "2024-09-01"
| stats count() by tenant_id, status
| sort -count
```
rafael: quick scan: a few large enterprise tenants have similar synchronous checks but only this tenant's workload has the bursty concurrency pattern. Others had occasional single-digit errors. So problem is amplified by tenant traffic pattern.
anita: created an incident ticket and recorded artifact links: s3://artifacts/incidents/RT-5610/ and attached sample core dumps. Ticket assigned to eng-runtime.
meera: can we add a dashboard tile showing per-runtime accept queue length and per-runtime pending goroutines? That would let us detect pre-crash piles.
tom: +1. I'll add a Grafana panel for runtime accept_queue and queue_depth. Also we should alert on sustained queue_depth > 100 for any runtime node.
support-jordan: customer will run a controlled blast in staging with the billing check enabled to try to repro after you patch. They'll coordinate windows.
rafal: (typo) sorry, rafael: noted. I'll work on a PR to add a soft timeout + breaker around billing-check in the runtime client for v2.8.0 and backport the quick timeout to v2.7.x as hotfix.
anita: final note: we avoided running a full node replacement since routing override and concurrency cap brought SLO back under. Keep incident open until runtime patch lands and we verify in staging.
sam_oncall_bot: SLO status: degraded -> recovered at 14:25 UTC after caps and routing override. Pager cleared.
meera: creating follow-up tickets: RB-1201 (circuit-breaker), RB-1202 (runtime crash runbook), RB-1203 (dashboard + alert). Linking to RT-5610.
anita: thanks everyone. I'll draft the short post-incident summary and include repro steps + suggested mitigations for support docs.
